clue.text: Keenly sentimental and increasingly amorous, I, before and after school

indicators.note: the school is to stand on both sides, once at the front and once at the back of what follows

blocks.note: SCH is the standard abbreviation for school
growing warmer in feeling
taken as written
the same abbreviation, used a second time

explanation.surface: A lovesick pupil grows ever more soppy at school, from first bell to last.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is borrowed from German (schwärmerisch), so the odd-looking consonant cluster is genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: Schwärmerisch is a borrowing from German meaning gushing or effusively enthusiastic, as Chambers glosses it.

clue.text: Cuppa for Jock? A hot cup’s brewed about right

indicators.note: brewing stirs and mixes things, so the letters are tossed about
about means going around something, so the jumble wraps another letter

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's tea: a hot cup, freshly brewed, just right.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock is a crossword nickname for a Scot, so the definition asks for a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stroupach is a Scots dialect word for a cup of tea, the drink a Jock would call his cuppa.

clue.text: Basset? Crowning feature in position

blocks.note: a crest tops a head or a hill
a switch or device that is on is in position

explanation.surface: A dog's crowning glory is in place, as at a show.
explanation.walkthrough: Basset suggests the hound, but here it is the geological term for an outcrop of rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A creston, like a basset, is a stratum of rock cropping out at the surface in mining terms.

clue.text: Appropriate in female, it may prompt immune response

indicators.note: one word sits inside the other, held within it

blocks.note: apt means fitting or suitable
a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: Something suitable within a woman's body may set off her immune defences.
explanation.definitionFit: A hapten is a small molecule that triggers antibody production once it is bound to a carrier protein.

clue.text: Stirring acts I sing about ring? Such this might have included

definitions.text: Stirring acts I sing about ring? Such this might have included

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the letters that follow are reordered
about means surrounding, so the mixed letters go round another

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A boxing ring with stirring acts and songs: such might be part of the contests.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: stirring acts in a ring are what athletic contests could include.
explanation.definitionFit: Agonistics is the art of athletic combat, the contests of ancient Greek games, which would feature rousing acts in a ring.

clue.text: One side of wagon? With that it’s shiny black

blocks.note: first meaning: a side rail or piece of a cart
second reading: with one side of the word wagon, its last letter, added, the word becomes a glossy black bird's colour

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reuses the first: one side of 'wagon' is its letter N, and RAVE plus N makes RAVEN, a shiny black.
explanation.definitionFit: A rave is the side piece of a cart or wagon; raven describes the glossy black of the bird's plumage.

clue.text: Brainwave you utter ultimately in climbing tropical tree

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each of the two words before it
in a down clue climbing means going upward, so the word reads from bottom to top
the selected letters go inside the turned word

blocks.note: the last letters of these two words
the akee is a tropical tree with edible fruit

explanation.surface: A bright idea comes to you as you shout from high in a tropical tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Eureka, Archimedes' cry on discovery, stands for a sudden inspiration or flash of insight.

clue.text: What’ll suggest clan literally conforming with others? (6, two words)

blocks.note: setter's reading: the answer split another way hints at the letters of a word for clan, a sept, shuffled
surface reading: keeping pace with everyone else

explanation.walkthrough: A sept is a clan; its letters rearranged spell the second word of the answer, so read literally the phrase hints at the clan's letters within it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in step is to march in time with others, hence to conform to the group.

clue.text: Hemp genus from Q I had planted in region not far from there, yielding …

indicators.note: something planted is set into the ground, so these letters go inside the region

blocks.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
SA is South Australia, the state next door to Queensland

explanation.surface: A grower in Queensland describes the hemp he planted nearby and what it yielded.
explanation.walkthrough: Q is Queensland; Sida includes the fibre plant known there as Queensland hemp. The ellipsis runs on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Sida is the mallow genus that includes plants grown for fibre, such as Queensland hemp.

clue.text: … Fibre, increasingly evasive by the sound of it

indicators.note: we are told to judge by how the words are spoken, not written

blocks.note: more coy, more shy and evasive

explanation.surface: Continuing from the hemp: the fibre seems ever more elusive.
explanation.definitionFit: Coir is the coarse fibre from coconut husks, used for matting and rope.

clue.text: Place to order pasta (cocotte sent back)

indicators.note: sending a dish back returns it the way it came, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: a cocotte is a prostitute, a tart

explanation.surface: A diner orders pasta but sends back the casserole dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Cocotte also means a little casserole dish, which suits the restaurant scene; here it is the old word for a loose woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A trat is an informal shortening of trattoria, an Italian restaurant where pasta is served.

clue.text: Nun dressed in reverse of black abroad? She was disapproved of

indicators.note: dressing arranges or treats something, so these letters are rearranged
the reverse of a word is that word read backwards
the rearranged letters go inside the turned word

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
noir is French for black

explanation.surface: A nun in a black habit in a foreign land fell from favour.
explanation.definitionFit: Runnion is a Shakespearean term of abuse for a woman, so it names someone regarded with contempt.

clue.text: Butter’s given a wee bittie salt? It provides more than we really want (10, two words)

definitions.text: It provides more than we really want

blocks.note: a butter is something that butts, such as a nanny goat
tate is a Scots word for a small portion

explanation.surface: Someone is handed a tiny pinch of salt for their butter, and complains it is too much.
explanation.walkthrough: Butter is a misdirection: it is one who butts, a goat. The salt link fits the theme, as nanny-state rules often target salt intake.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanny state is a government seen as overprotective, providing more interference than its citizens wish.

clue.text: One decrying member of travelling troupe?

blocks.note: a rep is a repertory company of actors
a rover is one who travels about

explanation.surface: Someone criticises a strolling player.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the split reading: a touring actor is a rover belonging to a rep company, a repertory troupe.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprover rebukes or censures, which is to decry someone's conduct.

clue.text: See me among waving reeds poking above the surface

indicators.note: to be among things is to be in their midst, so one piece sits inside another
things waving move about, so the letters are disturbed

blocks.note: taken as written
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Look at me standing among reeds swaying above the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Emersed is a botanical term for leaves or stems rising out of water.

clue.text: Punch sleuth allowed always to poets

blocks.note: a private eye is a detective
let means permitted
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: Mr Punch, the puppet, is a detective forever indulged by poets.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch is not the puppet or a blow but a tool for making holes.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyeleteer is a pointed instrument for piercing eyelet holes, a kind of punch.

clue.text: People dividing view, any, regarding apartment block

indicators.note: something dividing another splits it, sitting in its middle

blocks.note: men are people
a tenet is an opinion or belief
ary is a dialect form of any

explanation.surface: Residents disagree over the outlook from their block of flats.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenementary is the adjective relating to a tenement, a large building divided into flats.

clue.text: Sharing a ma but not a pa, i.e. with nature varied but not accepted

definitions.text: Sharing a ma but not a pa

indicators.note: accepted is abbreviated A, and but not tells us to take that letter out
something varied has been changed, so its letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
the word to be trimmed and mixed

explanation.surface: A half-sibling story: same mother, different father, a varied nature not accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: A is the abbreviation for accepted, so NATURE loses its A before mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: Uterine siblings are born of the same mother but different fathers, half-brothers or sisters on the maternal side.

clue.text: Student boozer, one joint incorporating another (not the first)

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter is dropped
to incorporate is to take something into one's body

blocks.note: the knee is a joint in the leg
the hip is another joint

explanation.surface: A student pub is a joint inside another joint, a dive within a dive.
explanation.walkthrough: Joint suggests a bar or dive, but here it is a body joint. KNEIPE is German for a tavern.
explanation.definitionFit: A Kneipe is a German student tavern or bar, the kind of pub where students drink.

clue.text: Lady’s mantle from the orient in puckered fabric

indicators.note: one letter sits inside the fabric's name

blocks.note: the orient is the east, E
plissé is a fabric with a puckered finish

explanation.surface: A lady's cloak from the East is made of crinkled cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady's mantle is also a garden plant, which the surface lets the solver half-expect.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelisse is a woman's long cloak or mantle, often fur-lined.

clue.text: Breaking stalk held up by officer briefly

indicators.note: in a down entry held up means raised, read from bottom to top
something held is grasped inside another

blocks.note: a seta is a stalk or bristle in botany
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: A broken plant stem is carried by a lieutenant for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: Breaking is an adjective here, as in breaking news.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking news is the very latest news, happening right now.

clue.text: Sum of little value one disowns

blocks.note: first meaning: an old French coin of small worth
second meaning: one who denies

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced differently: one rhymes with 'deny-er', the other with 'tenure'.
explanation.definitionFit: The denier was a French coin worth very little; a denier is also a person who denies or repudiates.

clue.text: I see the universe as complete in itself, lifting around length

definitions.text: I see the universe as complete in itself

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the lifting word wraps a letter

blocks.note: to hoist is to lift
L is the abbreviation for length

explanation.surface: A philosopher declares the cosmos self-sufficient while doing some heavy lifting.
explanation.definitionFit: A holist believes wholes are more than the sum of parts, seeing the cosmos as one complete system.

clue.text: Having what looks like hand one pair of bridge partners fed on

blocks.note: A as the indefinite article means one
North and South partner each other at bridge
ate means fed

explanation.surface: A bridge pair dine as the hand is played.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's last words read as fed on, but on is a link here; the definition plays on the Latin ansa, handle, which looks like hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Ansate means having a handle or a handle-shaped part, such as the looped ansate cross.

clue.text: Shortening (of speech), easy when half’s nicked, lifted

indicators.note: half of the word is taken away, stolen from it

blocks.note: the word to be halved
lifted means stolen, so stole

explanation.surface: Talk made easy once half of it is cut and pinched.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicked and lifted are both slang for stolen; the first is the deletion signal, the second the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody systole is the shortening of a naturally long syllable, a contraction in speech or verse.

clue.text: Like some breakfast? Against money being put into measure of grain once

indicators.note: put into means placed inside the following word

blocks.note: on can mean against, as in leaning on
tin is slang for money
a cental was a hundredweight of 100 pounds, used for grain

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about breakfast, against cash being poured into the grain bin.
explanation.definitionFit: A continental breakfast is a light European-style meal of rolls and coffee.

clue.text: Solid leader being somewhat demoted as formerly

indicators.note: demoted means moved down a little, so the letter leaves its top place

blocks.note: a cone is a geometric solid
the leader of the solid is its first letter

explanation.surface: A head of a firm is quietly demoted, as was done before.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the first letter of CONE drops two places, reading ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means at one time in the past, synonymous with formerly.

clue.text: Piece of wool after combing cat from tail up

indicators.note: starting at the tail and going up means reading the word from its end

blocks.note: a lion is a big cat

explanation.surface: Wool combed from the cat, working up from the tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Noil is the short fibre removed when wool is combed, a waste piece.

clue.text: Corner of Scotland to recognize up there having entered university

indicators.note: in a down entry going up means reading from the bottom
something that has entered is inside

blocks.note: ken is Scots for to know or recognise
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A Scottish nook you'd know up north, where a university has been set up.
explanation.walkthrough: Up there also hints at Scotland, being in the north of Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Neuk is the Scots form of nook, a corner, as in the East Neuk of Fife.

clue.text: Place on pedestal that is containing fantastic ladies

indicators.note: fantastic means wildly fanciful, so the word is rearranged
containing means holding something inside

blocks.note: i.e. stands for id est, that is
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Wonderful women are put up on a pedestal.
explanation.definitionFit: To idealise is to regard someone as perfect, to worship or exalt them.

clue.text: Scrap metal, inferior, including such as in Scotland, all returned

indicators.note: including means taking something inside
the whole thing is sent back, read backwards

blocks.note: less means lower in rank
sic is Scots for such

explanation.surface: Poor-quality metal from Scotland is all sent back.

clue.text: French art turning back on itself? It represents reality

indicators.note: turning back means retracing in the opposite direction, so the piece is read backwards

blocks.note: art is the old second person of be, which is es in French (tu es)
the same piece again, added onto itself

explanation.surface: French art folds back on itself to depict real life.
explanation.walkthrough: Art here is the archaic 'thou art', not painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Esse is the Latin-derived philosophical term for actual being or existence.

clue.text: Here, left and right, kettle’s boiling – confused?

indicators.note: boiling water churns, so the letters are tossed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left
R is the abbreviation for right
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Everything is everywhere, kettle boiling, the cook flustered.
explanation.definitionFit: Helter-skelter means in disorderly haste, in a confused rush.
